value: One of the two grapes allowed for red Carnuntum DAC, alongside Zweigelt, and always made dry.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Carnuntum: red DAC only from Zweigelt or Blaufränkisch (blends at least two thirds), dry, 12% minimum; Austrian Embassy Washington page: Carnuntum principal grapes Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch; WineAlign (commissioned by Austrian Wine Marketing Board): principal grapes include Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch.

value: One of the three grapes allowed for white Carnuntum DAC, with Weißburgunder and Grüner Veltliner, and always made dry.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Carnuntum: white DAC only from Chardonnay, Weißburgunder or Grüner Veltliner, dry; WineAlign (sponsored by Austrian Wine Marketing Board): Carnuntum principal grapes include Chardonnay.

value: One of the three grapes allowed for white Carnuntum DAC, with Chardonnay and Weißburgunder, in a region better known for its reds.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Carnuntum: white DAC from Chardonnay, Weißburgunder or Grüner Veltliner; Austrian Embassy: principal grapes Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch, Grüner Veltliner among others; WineAlign (sponsored): Grüner Veltliner among principal grapes.

value: Weißburgunder
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Carnuntum names the variety Weißburgunder; The Wine Society Austria guide uses weissburgunder (pinot blanc) for Austria.

value: One of the three grapes allowed for white Carnuntum DAC, with Chardonnay and Grüner Veltliner, and always made dry.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Carnuntum: white DAC from Chardonnay, Weißburgunder or Grüner Veltliner, dry; Austrian Embassy: Pinot Blanc grown in Carnuntum; WineAlign (sponsored): Weissburgunder a principal grape.

value: The only grape of regional Eisenberg DAC, always unblended and dry, and also allowed for its village and single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Eisenberg: Gebietswein 100 percent Blaufränkisch, no blending, max 4 g/l sugar; village and Ried wines Blaufränkisch or Welschriesling; Burgenland Tourismus: Eisenberg DAC stands for the typical Blaufränkisch; WineAlign (sponsored): principal grape Blaufränkisch.

value: Here it is fruity with a distinctly mineral spiciness, from loamy, mineral rich soils.
source_notes: Burgenland Tourismus: Eisenberg DAC Blaufränkisch fruity and mineral spicy, loamy mineral rich soils; WineAlign (sponsored by Austrian Wine Marketing Board): Eisenberg Blaufränkisch has a mineral spiciness.

value: With Riesling, one of the two traditional grapes of Kamptal DAC, allowed at every level from regional to single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Kamptal: Grüner Veltliner and Riesling (now also Chardonnay, Weißburgunder, Grauburgunder) at all three tiers; Weinstraße Kamptal: Grüner Veltliner and Riesling are the established Kamptal DAC grapes; The Wine Society: grüner and riesling the Kamptal DAC grapes.

value: Its single vineyard wines are medium to full bodied and spicy, with power and concentration but no heaviness.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Kamptal: Riedenwein medium to full style, spicy to moderately aromatic; The Wine Society: Kamptal single vineyard wines show power and concentration without heaviness.

value: With Grüner Veltliner, one of the two traditional grapes of Kamptal DAC, allowed at every level from regional to single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Kamptal: Riesling allowed at all three tiers; Weinstraße Kamptal: Grüner Veltliner and Riesling are the established Kamptal DAC grapes; The Wine Society: Riesling a Kamptal DAC grape.

value: With Riesling, one of the two grapes of Kremstal DAC, made dry from regional wines up to Reserve.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Kremstal: Grüner Veltliner or Riesling, dry, tiers up to Reserve; The Wine Society: grüner and riesling the core Kremstal grapes, premium dry wines labelled Reserve; Austrian Embassy: principal grapes Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

value: One of the four grapes of white Leithaberg DAC, with Weißburgunder, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner, made dry on its own or in a blend.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: white DAC from Weißer Burgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger or Grüner Veltliner or a blend, dry; The Wine Society: Leithaberg whites from chardonnay, grüner veltliner, weissburgunder and Neuburger.

value: Here it is tight knit, saline and mineral rather than fruity, with fresh acidity and little or no taste of oak.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: taste engmaschig, mineralisch, primary fruit subordinate, no to barely noticeable oak; The Wine Society: Leithaberg whites broad, saline, concentrated with excellent acidity; Burgenland Tourismus: whites distinctive for minerality.

value: One of the four grapes of white Leithaberg DAC, with Weißburgunder, Chardonnay and Neuburger, made dry on its own or in a blend.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: white DAC from Weißer Burgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger or Grüner Veltliner or a blend, dry; The Wine Society: Leithaberg whites from these four grapes.

value: Here it is tight knit, saline and mineral, with the fruit held in the background and little or no taste of oak.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: taste engmaschig, würzig, mineralisch, primary fruit subordinate, no to barely noticeable oak; The Wine Society: Leithaberg whites saline and concentrated with excellent acidity; Burgenland Tourismus: whites distinctive for minerality.

value: One of the four grapes of white Leithaberg DAC, with Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner, made dry on its own or in a blend.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: white DAC includes Weißer Burgunder, dry; The Wine Society: weissburgunder one of the Leithaberg white grapes; Austrian Embassy: Weißburgunder a principal Leithaberg grape.

value: Here it is fuller and more saline than usual, tight knit and mineral, with fresh acidity and little or no taste of oak.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: taste engmaschig, mineralisch, elegant, no to barely noticeable oak; The Wine Society: Leithaberg whites broad, saline, concentrated with excellent acidity; Burgenland Tourismus: whites distinctive for minerality.

value: Here it is elegant, tight knit and mineral, with a saline freshness and little or no taste of oak.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Leithaberg: taste elegant, engmaschig, würzig, mineralisch, no to barely noticeable oak; The Wine Society: Leithaberg reds full bodied, mineral and saline, with depth and freshness; Burgenland Tourismus: reds distinctive for minerality.

value: The only grape of Mittelburgenland DAC, made dry as Classic, single vineyard and Reserve wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Mittelburgenland: only Blaufränkisch, max 2.5 g/l sugar, Classic (little wood), Ried (little to slight wood), Reserve (noticeable to dominant wood); The Wine Society: Blaufränkisch the dominant grape of Mittelburgenland DAC; Burgenland Tourismus: region is Blaufränkisch country, DAC built on it.

value: Juicy and approachable in its Classic wines, while the single vineyard and Reserve wines are fuller and firmer and need time in bottle.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Mittelburgenland: Classic fruity and spicy; Ried and Reserve fruity, spicy and full bodied (kräftig); The Wine Society: entry level black fruited, spicy and juicy; top wines firm and dark, needing ageing to soften.

value: Welschriesling
source_notes: Austrian Embassy: Neusiedlersee principal grape Welschriesling, sweet BA and TBA from Welschriesling; WineAlign (sponsored): Neusiedlersee principal grape Welschriesling for sweet wines.

value: The only grape of red Neusiedlersee DAC, made dry and also as a fuller Reserve aged in large casks or barrique.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Neusiedlersee: dry red DAC and Reserve only from Zweigelt, Reserve aged in large traditional cask or barrique and kräftig; The Wine Society: Zweigelt the key Neusiedlersee DAC grape; Burgenland Tourismus: Neusiedlersee DAC stands for Zweigelt.

value: With Zweigelt, one of the two grapes of red Rosalia DAC, made on its own or blended with it.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Rosalia: red DAC from Blaufränkisch or Zweigelt, dry (max 4 g/l); Burgenland Tourismus: Rosalia DAC reds made from Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.

value: Rosalia DAC reds are deep in colour and full bodied, yet fine, with a delicate berry fruit.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Rosalia: taste finessenreich, fruchtig, würzig, aromatisch, colour kräftiges dunkles Rot; Burgenland Tourismus: Rosalia DAC reds extremely powerful and full bodied with a delicate berry aroma.

value: With Blaufränkisch, one of the two grapes of red Rosalia DAC, made on its own or blended with it.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Rosalia: red DAC from Blaufränkisch or Zweigelt; Burgenland Tourismus: Rosalia DAC reds made from Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.

value: Made as Rosalia DAC it is fuller than usual, deep in colour and full bodied, with a delicate berry fruit.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Rosalia: taste finessenreich, fruchtig, würzig, colour kräftiges dunkles Rot; Burgenland Tourismus: Rosalia DAC reds extremely powerful and full bodied with a delicate berry aroma.

value: Widely grown in Südsteiermark, where it is labelled Morillon and is one of the grapes allowed for Südsteiermark DAC.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Südsteiermark: Morillon on the list of permitted grapes; Wein Steiermark Südsteiermark page: Morillon, the Styrian Chardonnay, a notable share of plantings; WineAlign (sponsored): Chardonnay (Morillon) a principal grape.

value: Welschriesling
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Südsteiermark lists the variety as Welschriesling; Wein Steiermark Südsteiermark page names Welschriesling.

value: Widely grown in Südsteiermark and allowed for Südsteiermark DAC, mostly made into light, dry wines for everyday drinking.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Südsteiermark: Welschriesling permitted, max 4 g/l sugar; Wein Steiermark Südsteiermark page: Welschriesling one of the most planted grapes; Wein Steiermark Welschriesling page: easy drinking dry wines typical of Styria.

value: One of the main grapes of Südsteiermark, made dry under Südsteiermark DAC.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Südsteiermark: Muskateller permitted, max 4 g/l sugar; Austrian Embassy: Gelber Muskateller a principal Südsteiermark grape; Wine Folly: Styrian Muskateller an aromatic but dry Muscat; Wein Steiermark: Muskateller a notable share of plantings.

value: Widely grown in Südsteiermark and one of the grapes allowed for Südsteiermark DAC.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Südsteiermark: Weißburgunder on the permitted list; Wein Steiermark Südsteiermark page: Weißburgunder a notable share of plantings.

value: Fresh and fragrant with mouth watering acidity, showing elderflower, nettle and green pepper when picked early and grapefruit in riper wines.
source_notes: Wein Steiermark Südsteiermark page: early picked wines show elderflower, nettle and paprika, middle style grapefruit and passion fruit; Wine Folly: Styrian Sauvignon has mouth watering acidity with herbal notes; WineAlign (sponsored): fresh, fragrant Südsteiermark Sauvignon.

value: A Thermenregion DAC grape at every level up to single vineyard wines, and with St. Laurent a main red of the warmer south of the region.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Thermenregion: Blauburgunder allowed at regional, village and Ried level; WineAlign (sponsored): north known for whites, south mostly red, principal grapes include St. Laurent and Pinot Noir; Austrian Embassy: St. Laurent and Pinot Noir principal grapes.

value: Blauer Portugieser
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Thermenregion names the variety Blauer Portugieser; The Wine Society uses blauer portugieser for Austrian plantings.

value: A secondary red here, allowed only in regional Thermenregion DAC wines and not in village or single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Thermenregion: Blauer Portugieser permitted for Gebietswein only, not listed for Ortswein or Riedenwein; Austrian Embassy: Blauer Portugieser among the other (secondary) Thermenregion grapes.

value: A Thermenregion DAC grape at every level up to single vineyard wines, and with Pinot Noir a main red of the warmer south of the region.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Thermenregion: St. Laurent allowed at regional, village and Ried level; WineAlign (sponsored): south mostly red, St. Laurent a principal grape; Austrian Embassy: St. Laurent a principal grape.

value: A secondary red here, allowed in regional and village Thermenregion DAC wines but not in single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Thermenregion: Zweigelt permitted for Gebietswein and Ortswein, not listed for Riedenwein; Austrian Embassy: Zweigelt among the other (secondary) Thermenregion grapes.

value: With Riesling, one of the two grapes of Traisental DAC, made dry from regional wines up to Reserve.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Traisental: Grüner Veltliner or Riesling, dry, tiers up to Reserve; Austrian Embassy: principal grapes Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; WineAlign (sponsored): principal grapes Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

value: With Grüner Veltliner, one of the two grapes of Traisental DAC, made dry from regional wines up to Reserve.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Traisental: Grüner Veltliner or Riesling, dry, tiers up to Reserve; Austrian Embassy and WineAlign (sponsored): principal grapes Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

value: One of the main white grapes here and allowed for Vulkanland Steiermark DAC, where it is labelled Morillon.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Vulkanland Steiermark: Morillon on the permitted list; Austrian Embassy: Morillon (Chardonnay) a principal grape of Südoststeiermark; Wein Steiermark Vulkanland page: Morillon among the white grapes planted.

value: Widely grown here and allowed for Vulkanland Steiermark DAC, mostly made into light, dry wines released early.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Vulkanland Steiermark: Welschriesling permitted, earlier test number date and exempt from the sales date; Wein Steiermark Vulkanland page: Welschriesling the most planted variety; Wein Steiermark Welschriesling page: easy drinking dry wines; WineAlign (sponsored): a principal grape.

value: Allowed for Vulkanland Steiermark DAC, where it is made dry.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Vulkanland Steiermark: Muskateller permitted, max 4 g/l sugar; Wein Steiermark Vulkanland page: Gelber Muskateller among the white grapes; Wine Folly: Styrian Muskateller an aromatic but dry Muscat.

value: Widely grown here, and with Sauvignon Blanc a lead grape for Vulkanland Steiermark DAC village wines in several areas.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Vulkanland Steiermark: Weissburgunder a Leitsorte with Sauvignon blanc for Oststeiermark, Riegersburg, Kapfenstein and St. Peter; Wein Steiermark Vulkanland page: Weißburgunder second by area; WineAlign (sponsored): Sauvignon the Ortswein flagship with Pinot Blanc also important.

value: Allowed for Vulkanland Steiermark DAC only when made dry.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Vulkanland Steiermark: Riesling permitted and must be trocken; Wein Steiermark Vulkanland page: Riesling named only at the end of the list of white grapes, after Morillon.

value: With Riesling, one of the Wachau's two lead grapes, and the only two allowed for Wachau DAC single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Wachau: Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner or Riesling; Vinea Wachau: Riedenweine exclusively from the Wachau lead varieties Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; The Wine Society: the two most important Wachau grapes.

value: It runs from light Steinfeder to rich Smaragd, where it gains riper, more tropical fruit while the cool Danube nights keep it fresh.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Wachau Smaragd Grüner offers richer tropical fruit, Klassik styles lighter; The Wine Society: opulent Wachau wines, day night temperature swings keep acidity high; Vinea Wachau: Steinfeder light, Smaragd complex and long lived.

value: With Grüner Veltliner, one of the Wachau's two lead grapes, and the only two allowed for Wachau DAC single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Wachau: Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner or Riesling; Vinea Wachau: Riedenweine exclusively from Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; The Wine Society: the two most important Wachau grapes.

value: Its richer wines are dense in texture yet keep high acidity, and the best need some years in bottle and can age for decades.
source_notes: The Wine Society: Wachau wines often viscous, acidity kept high by Danube temperature swings, top examples age for decades and need a few years; Vinea Wachau: Smaragd complex and long lived (not grape specific).

value: Allowed only in regional Wachau DAC wines, since village and single vineyard wines must be white.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Wachau: Zweigelt permitted for Gebietswein, Ortswein list white only, Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner or Riesling; Vinea Wachau: Ortswein list of typical varieties all white, Riedenweine only Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

value: The main grape of Wagram, allowed at every level of Wagram DAC, including single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Wagram: Grüner Veltliner permitted for regional, village and Ried wines; The Wine Society: grüner and riesling make up most of Wagram; Donau Niederösterreich Tourismus: Grüner Veltliner sets the tone in quantity.

value: A secondary red here, allowed in regional and village Wagram DAC wines but not in single vineyard wines.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Wagram: Zweigelt permitted at regional and village level, Ried level only Grüner Veltliner, Roter Veltliner, Riesling; Austrian Embassy: Zweigelt among the other Wagram grapes; The Wine Society: zweigelt among the red varieties grown in Wagram.

value: The only grape of Weinviertel DAC, made as a light, unoaked classic wine and as a fuller Reserve and Große Reserve.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Weinviertel: only Grüner Veltliner, no oak in classic, Reserve kräftig, Große Reserve; Regionales Weinkomitee Weinviertel: Weinviertel DAC is always Grüner Veltliner, flagship grape; The Wine Society: nearly half of plantings, entry level wines.

value: In its classic form it is light and fresh with no oak, and the peppery note is so marked that locals call it Pfefferl.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Weinviertel: taste fruchtig, würzig, pfeffrig, no wood tone; Regionales Weinkomitee Weinviertel: pfeffrige Würze, light lively wines, Pfefferl; The Wine Society: signature pepper note, locally nicknamed Pfefferl.

value: Schilcher
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Weststeiermark: Blauer Wildbacher (ausgebaut als Schilcher), label term Schilcher Klassik; Wein Steiermark Weststeiermark page: rosé wines that are called Schilcher here.

value: The signature grape of Weststeiermark, allowed for Weststeiermark DAC only when made as Schilcher, a wine that may come from no other grape.
source_notes: RIS DAC Verordnung Weststeiermark: Blauer Wildbacher (ausgebaut als Schilcher), Leitsorte for village wines; Wein Steiermark: Schilcher may be made only from Blauer Wildbacher, central to the region; WineAlign (sponsored): Schilcher the region's star.

value: Weißburgunder
source_notes: Wiener Wein (Landwirtschaftskammer Wien) uses Weißburgunder; The Wine Society uses weissburgunder (pinot blanc) for Austria.

value: Regarded as a typically Viennese grape, made as a single variety wine and also found in the city's Gemischter Satz field blends.
source_notes: Wiener Wein: Weißburgunder gilt als typisch wienerisch; Wine Folly: Wiener Gemischter Satz varieties can include Pinot Blanc; Austrian Embassy: Weißburgunder among Vienna's grapes.
